text:
Devon: FYI seeing a correlated spike in scratchpool write latency & GPU preemptions around 09:03 UTC.
Devon: metrics: p95 write latency jumped from ~2ms -> 18ms, iops per-node peaked ~140k, provisioner started failing 15% of GPU attaches.
Ajay: ouch. Any recent jobs that would cause a rebalance or heavy fsyncs?
Devon: yes — nightly hotstripe rebalance kicked off at 09:00. It looks like it faned out writes across NVMe lanes and saturated IO queue depth.
Maria: can you link the grafana panel? also which region / pool?
Devon: https://graf.redwood/prod/scratchpool#range=09:00-09:15, affected pool: scratchpool-eu-west2-hotstripe
Devon: attached quick log snippet from node gnode-342:
```
fsync: 09:03:12 write latency spike: avg=18.2ms queue_depth=256 iops=138000
janitor: spawn 64 rewriter workers -> concurrent writes skyrocketed
kernel: blk_mq: dispatch latency increased
```
Sergey: sounds like rebalance concurrency + janitor rewrite overlap. We should cap rebalance workers and add backpressure to janitor.
Lina: +1. Also preemptions are from our GPU provisioning health check: attach waits > 5s -> preempt. If we throttle rewriter it should drop latency but will slow cleanup.
Ajay: tradeoff: delaying cleanup increases tempfile count and wear hotspots. How long is safe to delay? ballpark?
Maria: ops history suggests we can defer non-critical rebalances up to 6 hours during peak without impacting capacity for most tenants. Critical for older hotspots only.
Devon: current impact: ~120 attach failures in 15m window, mostly PLG namespaces. Revenue-sensitive but not a full outage.
Sergey: immediate mitigations:
- reduce rebalance parallelism from 64 -> 8 (hotfix)
- apply io cgroup write_bps throttle: systemd-run --scope -p BlockIOWriteBandwidth=/dev/nvme0n1:200M <janitor>
- schedule rebalance to low traffic window + stagger across sockets
Lina: can someone run the cgroup command on a small canary set? I'll coordinate oncall.
Devon: on it — will patch janitor config and restart process on 3 canaries: gnode-342/345/349
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2025-0811-001, severity: P2 — tagging eng-infra, eng-sre, product
Ajay: after throttle we should also add a check in the controller so future rebalances don't start when host iops > 90th percentile baseline.
Maria: agreed. Long term: enhance scheduler to check per-node storage pressure metric before starting heavy cleanup.
Devon: short-term patch deployed on canaries at 09:19. Observed p95 drop to ~3.5ms and attach failures stopped after ~4m.
Devon: rolling to remaining hosts now with concurrency 8.
Sergey: follow-ups (tracked on ticket):
- add storage pressure gating to rebalance job (owner: eng-infra)
- janitor: add max_concurrency per-socket and io-throttle flags (owner: eng-ml-cleaner)
- add alert for rebalance fanout causing iops > N per-node (owner: eng-sre)
Lina: also we should document cost impact: throttling increases cleanup window which may slightly raise total write amplification and wear; ops to quantify in ticket.
Devon: noted. closing loop: patch landed, metric panels updated, canary successful. Will post RCA & timeline in INC ticket.
oncall-bot: Reminder: postmortem due in 48h for P2 incidents unless waived.
Devon: thanks all :thumbsup:
